- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overhang.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates future values; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use moving average smoothing.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price shows mean-reversion pattern, model often fails to revert; apply a 3–5 day lag correction or use sentiment-weighted moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate volatility in low-sentiment periods; add 1–2% noise or adjust mean by +0.5–1.0 to account for suppressed momentum.
- If sentiment is declining (e.g., 0.6→0.2) and model forecast is rising, reverse direction: if sentiment drops below 0.3, reduce forecast slope or trigger downward bias correction.
